05.9a6c7ec809:
<n>53:3</n> Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
<n>53:4</n> Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
<n>53:5</n> Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
<n>53:6</n> Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
<n>53:7</n> Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
<n>53:8</n> Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
<n>53:9</n> Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
05.8018896c24:
<n>53:3</n> Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.
<n>53:4</n> O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.
<n>53:5</n> For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.
<n>53:6</n> For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.
<n>53:7</n> Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.
<n>53:8</n> I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:
<n>53:9</n> For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.
05.53ee802b60:
<n>50:3</n> Miserére mei, Deus, * secúndum magnam misericórdiam tuam.
<n>50:3</n> Et secúndum multitúdinem miseratiónum tuárum, * dele iniquitátem meam.
<n>50:4</n> Ámplius lava me ab iniquitáte mea: * et a peccáto meo munda me.
<n>50:5</n> Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: * et peccátum meum contra me est semper.
<n>50:6</n> Tibi soli peccávi, et malum coram te feci: * ut iustificéris in sermónibus tuis, et vincas cum iudicáris.
<n>50:7</n> Ecce enim, in iniquitátibus concéptus sum: * et in peccátis concépit me mater mea.
<n>50:8</n> Ecce enim, veritátem dilexísti: * incérta et occúlta sapiéntiæ tuæ manifestásti mihi.
<n>50:9</n> Aspérges me hyssópo, et mundábor: * lavábis me, et super nivem dealbábor.
<n>50:10</n> Audítui meo dabis gáudium et lætítiam: * et exsultábunt ossa humiliáta.
<n>50:11</n> Avérte fáciem tuam a peccátis meis: * et omnes iniquitátes meas dele.
<n>50:12</n> Cor mundum crea in me, Deus: * et spíritum rectum ínnova in viscéribus meis.
<n>50:13</n> Ne proícias me a fácie tua: * et spíritum sanctum tuum ne áuferas a me.
<n>50:14</n> Redde mihi lætítiam salutáris tui: * et spíritu principáli confírma me.
<n>50:15</n> Docébo iníquos vias tuas: * et ímpii ad te converténtur.
<n>50:16</n> Líbera me de sanguínibus, Deus, Deus salútis meæ: * et exsultábit lingua mea iustítiam tuam.
<n>50:17</n> Dómine, lábia mea apéries: * et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
<n>50:18</n> Quóniam si voluísses sacrifícium, dedíssem útique: * holocáustis non delectáberis.
<n>50:19</n> Sacrifícium Deo spíritus contribulátus: * cor contrítum, et humiliátum, Deus, non despícies.
<n>50:20</n> Benígne fac, Dómine, in bona voluntáte tua Sion: * ut ædificéntur muri Ierúsalem.
<n>50:21</n> Tunc acceptábis sacrifícium iustítiæ, oblatiónes, et holocáusta: * tunc impónent super altáre tuum vítulos.
05.78bd93ec68:
<n>50:3</n> Have mercy on me, O God, * according to thy great mercy.
<n>50:3</n> And according to the multitude of thy tender mercies * blot out my iniquity.
<n>50:4</n> Wash me yet more from my iniquity, * and cleanse me from my sin.
<n>50:5</n> For I know my iniquity, * and my sin is always before me.
<n>50:6</n> To thee only have I sinned, and have done evil before thee: * that thou mayst be justified in thy words, and mayst overcome when thou art judged.
<n>50:7</n> For behold I was conceived in iniquities; * and in sins did my mother conceive me.
<n>50:8</n> For behold thou hast loved truth: * the uncertain and hidden things of thy wisdom thou hast made manifest to me.
<n>50:9</n> Thou shalt sprinkle me with hyssop, and I shall be cleansed: * thou shalt wash me, and I shall be made whiter than snow.
<n>50:10</n> To my hearing thou shalt give joy and gladness: * and the bones that have been humbled shall rejoice.
<n>50:11</n> Turn away thy face from my sins, * and blot out all my iniquities.
<n>50:12</n> Create a clean heart in me, O God: * and renew a right spirit within my bowels.
<n>50:13</n> Cast me not away from thy face; * and take not thy holy spirit from me.
<n>50:14</n> Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, * and strengthen me with a perfect spirit.
<n>50:15</n> I will teach the unjust thy ways: * and the wicked shall be converted to thee.
<n>50:16</n> Deliver me from blood, O God, thou God of my salvation: * and my tongue shall extol thy justice.
<n>50:17</n> O Lord, thou wilt open my lips: * and my mouth shall declare thy praise.
<n>50:18</n> For if thou hadst desired sacrifice, I would indeed have given it: * with burnt offerings thou wilt not be delighted.
<n>50:19</n> A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit: * a contrite and humbled heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.
<n>50:20</n> Deal favourably, O Lord, in thy good will with Sion; * that the walls of Jerusalem may be built up.
<n>50:21</n> Then shalt thou accept the sacrifice of justice, oblations and whole burnt offerings: * then shall they lay calves upon thy altar.
05.42a7bca5e2:
<n>51:3</n> Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
<n>51:4</n> Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
<n>51:5</n> Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
<n>51:6</n> Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
<n>51:7</n> Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
<n>51:8</n> Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:
<n>51:9</n> Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
<n>51:10</n> Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
<n>51:11</n> Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
05.a9488cebd9:
<n>51:3</n> Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?
<n>51:4</n> All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.
<n>51:5</n> Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.
<n>51:6</n> Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.
<n>51:7</n> Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.
<n>51:8</n> The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:
<n>51:9</n> But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.
<n>51:10</n> But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.
<n>51:11</n> I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.
05.f6919c52be:
<n>52:1</n> Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
<n>52:2</n> Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
<n>52:3</n> Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
<n>52:4</n> Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
<n>52:5</n> Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
<n>52:6</n> Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
<n>52:6</n> Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
<n>52:7</n> Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
05.5e1a154d0f:
<n>52:1</n> The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.
<n>52:2</n> They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.
<n>52:3</n> God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.
<n>52:4</n> All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.
<n>52:5</n> Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?
<n>52:6</n> They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.
<n>52:6</n> For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.
<n>52:7</n> Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.
05.1de3ec58b3:
<n>54:2</n> Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.
<n>54:3</n> Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.
<n>54:4</n> Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.
<n>54:5</n> Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.
<n>54:6</n> Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.
<n>54:7</n> Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?
<n>54:8</n> Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.
<n>54:9</n> Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.
<n>54:10</n> Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.
<n>54:11</n> Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros eius iníquitas: * et labor in médio eius, et iniustítia.
<n>54:12</n> Et non defécit de platéis eius * usúra, et dolus.
<n>54:13</n> Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.
<n>54:13</n> Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.
<n>54:14</n> Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:
<n>54:15</n> Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.
<n>54:16</n> Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:
<n>54:16</n> Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.
05.1ebae513c0:
<n>54:2</n> Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication: * be attentive to me and hear me.
<n>54:3</n> I am grieved in my exercise; * and am troubled, at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner.
<n>54:4</n> For they have cast iniquities upon me; * and in wrath they were troublesome to me.
<n>54:5</n> My heart is troubled within me: * and the fear of death is fallen upon me.
<n>54:6</n> Fear and trembling are come upon me: * and darkness hath covered me.
<n>54:7</n> And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?
<n>54:8</n> Lo, I have gone far off flying away; * and I abode in the wilderness.
<n>54:9</n> I waited for him that hath saved me * from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.
<n>54:10</n> Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.
<n>54:11</n> Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: * and in the midst thereof are labour, and injustice.
<n>54:12</n> And usury and deceit * have not departed from its streets.
<n>54:13</n> For if my enemy had reviled me, * I would verily have borne with it.
<n>54:13</n> And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, * I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.
<n>54:14</n> But thou a man of one mind, * my guide, and my familiar.
<n>54:15</n> Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: * in the house of God we walked with consent.
<n>54:16</n> Let death come upon them, * and let them go down alive into hell.
<n>54:16</n> For there is wickedness in their dwellings: * in the midst of them.
05.68148d90d3:
<n>54:17</n> Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.
<n>54:18</n> Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.
<n>54:19</n> Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.
<n>54:20</n> Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.
<n>54:20</n> Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.
<n>54:21</n> Contaminavérunt testaméntum eius, divísi sunt ab ira vultus eius: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.
<n>54:22</n> Mollíti sunt sermónes eius super óleum: * et ipsi sunt iácula.
<n>54:23</n> Iacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem iusto.
<n>54:24</n> Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.
<n>54:24</n> Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.
05.5e6ec5bed9:
<n>54:17</n> But I have cried to God: * and the Lord will save me.
<n>54:18</n> Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: * and he shall hear my voice.
<n>54:19</n> He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: * for among many they were with me.
<n>54:20</n> God shall hear, * and the Eternal shall humble them.
<n>54:20</n> For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: * he hath stretched forth his hand to repay.
<n>54:21</n> They have defiled his covenant, they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, * and his heart hath drawn near.
<n>54:22</n> His words are smoother than oil, * and the same are darts.
<n>54:23</n> Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: * he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.
<n>54:24</n> But thou, O God, shalt bring them down * into the pit of destruction.
<n>54:24</n> Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; * but I will trust in thee, O Lord.
05.725960e5e1:
<n>55:2</n> Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
<n>55:3</n> Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
<n>55:4</n> Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.
<n>55:5</n> In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
<n>55:6</n> Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.
<n>55:7</n> Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.
<n>55:8</n> Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.
<n>55:9</n> Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
<n>55:9</n> Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:
<n>55:10</n> In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.
<n>55:11</n> In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
<n>55:12</n> In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.
<n>55:13</n> Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.
05.040ae59188:
<n>55:2</n> Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.
<n>55:3</n> My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.
<n>55:4</n> From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.
<n>55:5</n> In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.
<n>55:6</n> All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.
<n>55:7</n> They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.
<n>55:8</n> As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.
<n>55:9</n> O God, I have declared to thee my life: * thou hast set my tears in thy sight,
<n>55:9</n> As also in thy promise. * Then shall my enemies be turned back.
<n>55:10</n> In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * behold I know thou art my God.
<n>55:11</n> In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. * In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.
<n>55:12</n> In me, O God, are vows to thee, * which I will pay, praises to thee:
<n>55:13</n> Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: * that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.
05.a2c0b5869a:
<n>56:2</n> Miserére mei, Deus, miserére mei: * quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.
<n>56:2</n> Et in umbra alárum tuárum sperábo, * donec tránseat iníquitas.
<n>56:3</n> Clamábo ad Deum altíssimum: * Deum qui benefécit mihi.
<n>56:4</n> Misit de cælo, et liberávit me: * dedit in oppróbrium conculcántes me.
<n>56:4</n> Misit Deus misericórdiam suam, et veritátem suam, * et erípuit ánimam meam de médio catulórum leónum: dormívi conturbátus.
<n>56:5</n> Fílii hóminum dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: * et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
<n>56:6</n> Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, * et in omnem terram glória tua.
<n>56:7</n> Láqueum paravérunt pédibus meis: * et incurvavérunt ánimam meam.
<n>56:7</n> Fodérunt ante fáciem meam fóveam: * et incidérunt in eam.
<n>56:8</n> Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam.
<n>56:9</n> Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
<n>56:10</n> Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psalmum dicam tibi in géntibus:
<n>56:11</n> Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos misericórdia tua, * et usque ad nubes véritas tua.
<n>56:12</n> Exaltáre super cælos, Deus: * et super omnem terram glória tua.
05.9f613fa0b3:
<n>56:2</n> Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me: * for my soul trusteth in thee.
<n>56:2</n> And in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, * until iniquity pass away.
<n>56:3</n> I will cry to God the most High; * to God who hath done good to me.
<n>56:4</n> He hath sent from heaven and delivered me: * he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me.
<n>56:4</n> God hath sent his mercy and his truth, * and he hath delivered my soul from the midst of the young lions. I slept troubled.
<n>56:5</n> The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, * and their tongue a sharp sword.
<n>56:6</n> Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, * and thy glory above all the earth.
<n>56:7</n> They prepared a snare for my feet; * and they bowed down my soul.
<n>56:7</n> They dug a pit before my face, * and they are fallen into it.
<n>56:8</n> My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and rehearse a psalm.
<n>56:9</n> Arise, O my glory, arise psaltery and harp: * I will arise early.
<n>56:10</n> I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people: * I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations.
<n>56:11</n> For thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens: * and thy truth unto the clouds.
<n>56:12</n> Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: * and thy glory above all the earth.
05.bc17c960b9:
<n>57:2</n> Si vere útique iustítiam loquímini: * recta iudicáte, fílii hóminum.
<n>57:3</n> Étenim in corde iniquitátes operámini: * in terra iniustítias manus vestræ concínnant.
<n>57:4</n> Alienáti sunt peccatóres a vulva, erravérunt ab útero: * locúti sunt falsa.
<n>57:5</n> Furor illis secúndum similitúdinem serpéntis: * sicut áspidis surdæ, et obturántis aures suas,
<n>57:6</n> Quæ non exáudiet vocem incantántium: * et venéfici incantántis sapiénter.
<n>57:7</n> Deus cónteret dentes eórum in ore ipsórum: * molas leónum confrínget Dóminus.
<n>57:8</n> Ad níhilum devénient tamquam aqua decúrrens: * inténdit arcum suum donec infirméntur.
<n>57:9</n> Sicut cera, quæ fluit, auferéntur: * supercécidit ignis, et non vidérunt solem.
<n>57:10</n> Priúsquam intellégerent spinæ vestræ rhamnum: * sicut vivéntes, sic in ira absórbet eos.
<n>57:11</n> Lætábitur iustus cum víderit vindíctam: * manus suas lavábit in sánguine peccatóris.
<n>57:12</n> Et dicet homo: Si útique est fructus iusto: * útique est Deus iúdicans eos in terra.
05.ed9ec4f6b4:
<n>57:2</n> If in very deed you speak justice: * judge right things, ye sons of men.
<n>57:3</n> For in your heart you work iniquity: * your hands forge injustice in the earth.
<n>57:4</n> The wicked are alienated from the womb; they have gone astray from the womb: * they have spoken false things.
<n>57:5</n> Their madness is according to the likeness of a serpent: * like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ears:
<n>57:6</n> Which will not hear the voice of the charmers; * nor of the wizard that charmeth wisely.
<n>57:7</n> God shall break in pieces their teeth in their mouth: * the Lord shall break the grinders of the lions.
<n>57:8</n> They shall come to nothing, like water running down; * he hath bent his bow till they be weakened.
<n>57:9</n> Like wax that melteth they shall be taken away: * fire hath fallen on them, and they shall not see the sun.
<n>57:10</n> Before your thorns could know the brier; he swalloweth them up, * as alive, in his wrath.
<n>57:11</n> The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge: * he shall wash his hands in the blood of the sinner.
<n>57:12</n> And man shall say: If indeed there be fruit to the just: * there is indeed a God that judgeth them on the earth.
05.77a5386859:
<n>58:2</n> Éripe me de inimícis meis, Deus meus: * et ab insurgéntibus in me líbera me.
<n>58:3</n> Éripe me de operántibus iniquitátem: * et de viris sánguinum salva me.
<n>58:4</n> Quia ecce cepérunt ánimam meam: * irruérunt in me fortes.
<n>58:5</n> Neque iníquitas mea, neque peccátum meum, Dómine: * sine iniquitáte cucúrri, et diréxi.
<n>58:6</n> Exsúrge in occúrsum meum, et vide: * et tu, Dómine, Deus virtútum, Deus Israël,
<n>58:6</n> Inténde ad visitándas omnes gentes: * non misereáris ómnibus, qui operántur iniquitátem.
<n>58:7</n> Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
<n>58:8</n> Ecce, loquéntur in ore suo, et gládius in lábiis eórum: * quóniam quis audívit?
<n>58:9</n> Et tu, Dómine, deridébis eos: * ad níhilum dedúces omnes gentes.
<n>58:10</n> Fortitúdinem meam ad te custódiam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia eius prævéniet me.
05.bd19aab4a3:
<n>58:2</n> Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; * and defend me from them that rise up against me.
<n>58:3</n> Deliver me from them that work iniquity, * and save me from bloody men.
<n>58:4</n> For behold they have caught my soul: * the mighty have rushed in upon me:
<n>58:5</n> Neither is it my iniquity, nor my sin, O Lord: * without iniquity have I run, and directed my steps.
<n>58:6</n> Rise up thou to meet me, and behold: * even thou, O Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel.
<n>58:6</n> Attend to visit all the nations: * have no mercy on all them that work iniquity.
<n>58:7</n> They shall return at evening, and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.
<n>58:8</n> Behold they shall speak with their mouth, and a sword is in their lips: * for who, say they, hath heard us?
<n>58:9</n> But thou, O Lord, shalt laugh at them: * thou shalt bring all the nations to nothing.
<n>58:10</n> I will keep my strength to thee: for thou art my protector: * my God, his mercy shall prevent me.
05.ac23440f27:
<n>58:12</n> Deus osténdet mihi super inimícos meos, ne occídas eos: * nequándo obliviscántur pópuli mei.
<n>58:12</n> Dispérge illos in virtúte tua: * et depóne eos, protéctor meus, Dómine:
<n>58:13</n> Delíctum oris eórum, sermónem labiórum ipsórum: * et comprehendántur in supérbia sua.
<n>58:13</n> Et de exsecratióne et mendácio annuntiabúntur in consummatióne: * in ira consummatiónis, et non erunt.
<n>58:14</n> Et scient quia Deus dominábitur Iacob: * et fínium terræ.
<n>58:15</n> Converténtur ad vésperam: et famem patiéntur ut canes, * et circuíbunt civitátem.
<n>58:16</n> Ipsi dispergéntur ad manducándum: * si vero non fúerint saturáti, et murmurábunt.
<n>58:17</n> Ego autem cantábo fortitúdinem tuam: * et exsultábo mane misericórdiam tuam.
<n>58:17</n> Quia factus es suscéptor meus, * et refúgium meum, in die tribulatiónis meæ.
<n>58:18</n> Adiútor meus, tibi psallam, quia, Deus, suscéptor meus es: * Deus meus, misericórdia mea.
05.3dc7947afa:
<n>58:12</n> God shall let me see over my enemies: slay them not, * lest at any time my people forget.
<n>58:12</n> And scatter them by thy power; * and bring them down, O Lord, my protector:
<n>58:13</n> For the sin of their mouth, and the word of their lips: * and let them be taken in their pride.
<n>58:13</n> And for their cursing and lying they shall be talked of, when they are consumed: * when they are consumed by thy wrath, and they shall be no more.
<n>58:14</n> And they shall know that God will rule Jacob, * and all the ends of the earth.
<n>58:15</n> They shall return at evening and shall suffer hunger like dogs: * and shall go round about the city.
<n>58:16</n> They shall be scattered abroad to eat, * and shall murmur if they be not filled.
<n>58:17</n> But I will sing thy strength: * and will extol thy mercy in the morning.
<n>58:17</n> For thou art become my support, * and my refuge, in the day of my trouble.
<n>58:18</n> Unto thee, O my helper, will I sing, for thou art God my defence: * my God my mercy.
05.ab767da567:
<n>59:3</n> Deus, repulísti nos, et destruxísti nos: * irátus es, et misértus es nobis.
<n>59:4</n> Commovísti terram, et conturbásti eam: * sana contritiónes eius, quia commóta est.
<n>59:5</n> Ostendísti pópulo tuo dura: * potásti nos vino compunctiónis.
<n>59:6</n> Dedísti metuéntibus te significatiónem: * ut fúgiant a fácie arcus:
<n>59:7</n> Ut liberéntur dilécti tui: * salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me.
<n>59:8</n> Deus locútus est in sancto suo: * lætábor, et partíbor Síchimam: et convállem tabernaculórum metíbor.
<n>59:9</n> Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim fortitúdo cápitis mei.
<n>59:9</n> Iuda rex meus: * Moab olla spei meæ.
<n>59:10</n> In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ súbditi sunt.
<n>59:11</n> Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
<n>59:12</n> Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos? * et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
<n>59:13</n> Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
<n>59:14</n> In Deo faciémus virtútem: * et ipse ad níhilum dedúcet tribulántes nos.
05.20098d0f66:
<n>59:3</n> God, thou hast cast us off, and hast destroyed us; * thou hast been angry, and hast had mercy on us.
<n>59:4</n> Thou hast moved the earth, and hast troubled it: * heal thou the breaches thereof, for it has been moved.
<n>59:5</n> Thou hast shewn thy people hard things; * thou hast made us drink the wine of sorrow.
<n>59:6</n> Thou hast given a warning to them that fear thee: * that they may flee from before the bow:
<n>59:7</n> That thy beloved may be delivered. * Save me with thy right hand, and hear me.
<n>59:8</n> God hath spoken in his holy place: * I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem; and will mete out the vale of tabernacles.
<n>59:9</n> Galaad is mine, and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim is the strength of my head.
<n>59:9</n> Juda is my king: * Moab is the pot of my hope.
<n>59:10</n> Into Edom will I stretch out my shoe: * to me the foreigners are made subject.
<n>59:11</n> Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?
<n>59:12</n> Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go out with our armies?
<n>59:13</n> Give us help from trouble: * for vain is the salvation of man.
<n>59:14</n> Through God we shall do mightily: * and he shall bring to nothing them that afflict us.
